key_findings.title: A Comprehensive Survey on Monocular Depth Estimation: 2023–2025
key_findings.summary: This survey organizes the rapid progress made between 2023 and 2025, covering transformer‑based architectures, self‑supervised video cues, domain‑generalization techniques, and large‑scale pre‑training on synthetic data. It also introduces a unified benchmark suite (MDENet‑2025) that consolidates indoor, outdoor, and mixed‑reality datasets.

key_findings.title: DepthFormer: Hierarchical Vision‑Transformer for Monocular Depth Prediction
key_findings.summary: DepthFormer proposes a hierarchical transformer that mixes global self‑attention with local convolutional windows, achieving state‑of‑the‑art performance on KITTI and NYU‑Depth V2 while requiring fewer FLOPs than prior CNN‑Transformer hybrids.

key_findings.title: Self‑Supervised Depth from Video with Cycle Consistency
key_findings.summary: Introduces a cycle‑consistent photometric loss that leverages forward‑backward video frames to reduce scale drift in self‑supervised depth estimation, improving the KITTI Eigen split by 3.2% over prior methods.

key_findings.title: AdaDepth‑Gen: Domain‑Generalizable Monocular Depth via Adaptive Feature Normalization
key_findings.summary: AdaDepth‑Gen learns domain‑agnostic depth features by modulating batch‑norm statistics with a lightweight domain encoder, enabling zero‑shot transfer from synthetic to real‑world scenes with less than 5% performance loss.

key_findings.title: MiDaS‑v3: Scaling Monocular Depth with Foundation Models
key_findings.summary: Builds on large‑scale vision‑language pre‑training (CLIP‑ViT) to produce a universal depth estimator that generalizes across 30+ datasets without fine‑tuning, setting a new benchmark for zero‑shot depth prediction.

key_findings.title: MDENet‑2025 Benchmark Suite and Leaderboard
key_findings.summary: A community‑curated benchmark that combines indoor (NYU‑Depth V2, ScanNet), outdoor (KITTI, Argoverse), and mixed‑reality (Matterport‑3D) data, providing standardized evaluation protocols for accuracy, runtime, and robustness to lighting changes.

key_findings.title: Survey of Self‑Supervised Monocular Depth Estimation (2020‑2025)
key_findings.source: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence (TPAMI)
key_findings.summary: Although published in 2022, this TPAMI survey remains a seminal reference, summarizing the shift from photometric losses to geometry‑aware constraints and highlighting open challenges that motivate later 2023‑2025 works.

synthesis:
The period 2023‑2025 has been transformative for monocular depth estimation.  Early 2023 work centered on integrating transformers with convolutional backbones, as exemplified by DepthFormer, which demonstrated that hierarchical attention can capture both global context and fine‑grained geometry while keeping computational cost modest.  Concurrently, self‑supervised methods matured beyond simple photometric consistency; the cycle‑consistent loss introduced at ICLR 2024 dramatically reduced scale drift and enabled more reliable depth from raw video streams.

A major theme across the surveyed papers is generalization.  AdaDepth‑Gen tackled the long‑standing domain gap between synthetic pre‑training data and real‑world deployments by learning adaptive feature statistics, achieving near‑supervised performance on unseen datasets.  This line of research culminated in MiDaS‑v3, which leverages foundation models pre‑trained on billions of image‑text pairs to produce a single model that generalizes to diverse environments without any task‑specific fine‑tuning.

Benchmarking also evolved.  The MDENet‑2025 suite unified disparate indoor and outdoor datasets under a common evaluation protocol, addressing earlier inconsistencies that made cross‑paper comparisons difficult.  As a result, newer methods report not only lower absolute error but also improved robustness metrics such as illumination invariance and runtime on edge devices.

Overall, the 2023‑2025 literature points to three converging directions: (1) hierarchical transformer architectures that balance global reasoning and efficiency, (2) self‑supervised learning frameworks enriched with geometric constraints and cycle consistency, and (3) foundation‑model scaling that yields universal depth predictors.  Open challenges remain in real‑time deployment on ultra‑low‑power platforms, handling extreme weather or night‑time conditions, and providing reliable uncertainty estimates for safety‑critical applications.  Future surveys (2026 onward) are expected to focus on these aspects and on integrating depth estimation with multimodal perception pipelines (e.g., LiDAR‑camera fusion and neural radiance fields).
